definition_en: to use something fully and well; to treat someone unfairly for gain; to develop a resource; a bold or remarkable deed
core_image: 把一份力量或资源使劲用出来
scene: 公司被指控剥削外来工人。 The company was accused of exploiting migrant workers.
sceneCN: 这里 exploit 是「剥削」（第 2 个义项）；句意：公司被指控剥削外来工人。

senses.title: Use well
senses.definition: to use something fully and well
senses.definitionCN: 充分而有效地利用某物
senses.example: We should exploit solar energy in this region.
senses.exampleCN: 我们应当在这个地区利用太阳能。
senses.why: The base sense is putting power to use.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是把力量用起来。

senses.title: Take unfair advantage
senses.definition: to treat someone unfairly for your own gain
senses.definitionCN: 为了自身利益不公正地对待他人
senses.example: The factory exploited young workers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂剥削年轻工人。
senses.why: Using turns into using people unfairly.
senses.whyCN: 「利用」变成不公正地利用人。

senses.title: Develop a resource
senses.definition: to develop a natural resource for use
senses.definitionCN: 开发自然资源以供使用
senses.example: The country began to exploit its oil fields.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家开始开发其油田。
senses.why: Using extends to large-scale resource work.
senses.whyCN: 利用扩展到大规模的资源开发。

senses.title: Bold deed
senses.definition: a bold or remarkable act
senses.definitionCN: 大胆而出色的行为
senses.example: The sailor told stories of his exploits at sea.
senses.exampleCN: 那位水手讲述他海上的英勇事迹。
senses.why: The noun keeps the old sense of an achievement.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了「成就」的古老含义。

intro.en: Exploit comes from Old French esploit, an achievement or success.
intro.cn: exploit 源自古法语 esploit，意为「成就、成功」。

items.en: Explicare means to unfold or set out.
items.cn: explicare 意为展开、铺陈。

items.en: Esploit means a success or bold deed.
items.cn: esploit 意为成功或英勇事迹。

items.en: Exploit first names a remarkable act.
items.cn: exploit 最初指非凡之举。

items.en: The verb exploit means to put to use.
items.cn: 动词 exploit 表示加以利用。

items.en: Exploit gains the negative sense of unfair use.
items.cn: exploit 获得「不公正利用」的负面含义。

note.en: Exploit is to use or take advantage; explore is to search.
note.cn: exploit 是利用或榨取，explore 则是探索。

entries.definition: to travel through to learn
to burst with force
to sell goods abroad
to make practical use of
to use wrongly or cruelly
to control and use a force

normalIntro.en: Exploit can mean use well, use badly, or a daring deed.
normalIntro.cn: exploit 既可指善加利用，也可指不正当地榨取，还可指英勇事迹。

normal.en: The farm exploits every hour of sunlight.
normal.cn: 这座农场充分利用每一小时阳光。

normal.en: Some employers exploit workers who lack papers.
normal.cn: 有些雇主剥削没有证件的工人。

normal.en: The firm plans to exploit the new oil field.
normal.cn: 公司计划开发新油田。

normal.en: She exploited her chance to study abroad.
normal.cn: 她抓住了出国留学的机会。

normal.en: The book tells of the explorer's exploits.
normal.cn: 这本书讲述了这位探险家的功绩。

abstract.en: Picture a tool used until it is worn thin.
abstract.cn: 想象一件工具被用到磨损。

abstract.en: Imagine a strong hand pressing down on someone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只强手向下压住别人。

abstract.en: Think of a medal won by a daring act.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚因英勇行为获得的奖章。

examples.en: The team exploited a weakness in the defense.
examples.cn: 这支队伍利用了防守中的弱点。

examples.en: Children should not be exploited for cheap labor.
examples.cn: 不应利用童工获取廉价劳动力。

examples.en: His exploits during the rescue won him a medal.
examples.cn: 他在救援中的英勇事迹为他赢得了一枚奖章。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exploit」联想 ex（出）+ ploit（用）：把别人的价值使劲用出来，就是「利用、剥削」。

root: 源自古法语 esploit（成就、事迹），可追溯到拉丁语 explicare（展开），核心义从「做成大事」演变为「加以利用」。

sensesIntro.en: Exploit means to use well, to take unfair advantage, to develop a resource, or a bold deed.
sensesIntro.cn: exploit 意为善加利用、剥削他人、开发资源，或英勇事迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: putting a force or person to full use.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一种力量或一个人用到底。

branches.en: The base verb sense is using something well.
branches.cn: 基础动词义是充分利用。

branches.en: Using people becomes unfair exploitation.
branches.cn: 利用人变成不公正的剥削。

branches.en: Using extends to developing resources.
branches.cn: 利用扩展到资源开发。

branches.en: The noun keeps the old sense of a bold deed.
branches.cn: 名词保留「英勇事迹」的旧义。

branches.en: Both concern extracting value, from people or land.
branches.cn: 两者都涉及从人或土地中榨取价值。

intro.en: Exploit comes through Old French from Latin explicare.
intro.cn: exploit 经古法语来自拉丁语 explicare。

latinIntro.en: Latin explicare, to unfold, lies behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 explicare（展开）是这个词的根源。

items.exampleCN: explicare 是 exploit 的根源。

items.example: Exploit keeps the sense of using.

definition_zh: 踝；脚踝；踝部（衣物或水面达到的高度）
definition_en: the joint between the foot and the leg, or the narrow part of the leg just above the foot
core_image: 脚跟上方突出的那节骨节
scene: 他跳下台阶时脚一歪，痛得蹲了下去。 She twisted her ankle on the icy steps.
sceneCN: 这里 ankle 是「脚踝」（第 1 个义项：脚与小腿相接的关节）；句意是她在结冰的台阶上扭伤了脚踝。

senses.title: The joint itself
senses.definition: the joint that connects the foot to the leg, where the leg narrows above the heel
senses.definitionCN: 连接脚与小腿的关节，位于脚跟上方小腿变窄处
senses.example: She twisted her ankle on the icy steps.
senses.exampleCN: 她在结冰的台阶上扭伤了脚踝。
senses.why: Ankle is a Germanic word for the bend of the leg, so it names the joint where the foot turns.
senses.whyCN: ankle 是日耳曼语中表示腿部弯折处的词，因此指脚转向的那个关节。

senses.title: The narrow part above the foot
senses.titleCN: 踝部（衣物或水达到的位置）
senses.definition: the narrow part of the leg just above the foot, used of clothing, socks, or the depth of water
senses.definitionCN: 脚上方小腿的狭窄部位，用于描述衣物、袜子或水的深度
senses.example: The water was ankle-deep after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨后，水只没到脚踝那么深。
senses.why: Because the joint is the lowest narrow point of the leg, the same word measures how high socks, boots, or water reach.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个关节是腿部最低的窄处，同一个词便用来量袜子、靴子或水到达的高度。

intro.en: Ankle is an old Germanic word for the bend of the leg, and it is a distant cousin of angle.
intro.cn: ankle 是日耳曼语中表示腿部弯折处的老词，与 angle 是远亲。

items.en: ankulaz meant 'ankle', built on a root for 'bend, angle'.
items.cn: ankulaz 意为「踝」，由表示「弯折、角」的词根构成。

items.en: The Old English form anclēow already meant the ankle joint.
items.cn: 古英语形式 anclēow 已指踝关节。

items.en: The word shrank to ankle, losing its older ending.
items.cn: 这个词缩略为 ankle，失去了较早的词尾。

items.en: Ankle is recorded in the fourteenth century with its modern spelling.
items.cn: ankle 在十四世纪已有现代拼写的记录。

items.en: Compounds such as ankle socks and ankle-deep turn the joint into a measure of height.
items.cn: ankle socks 与 ankle-deep 等复合词把这个关节变成高度的量度。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words built on the same bend-root; the near-meaning group holds other body joints.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「弯折」词根构成的词；近义组收其他身体关节。

entries.definition: a corner, or the space between two lines
a small ornament worn around the ankle
the bone of the ankle
the joint between the hand and the arm
the back part of the foot
a place where two bones meet

normalIntro.en: Ankle and angle both go back to a word for a bend.
normalIntro.cn: ankle 与 angle 都上溯到表示「弯折」的词。

normal.en: Ankle and angle share the idea of a bend.
normal.cn: ankle 与 angle 共享「弯折」这一概念。

normal.en: Twist your ankle is the usual injury phrase.
normal.cn: twist your ankle 是常见的受伤说法。

normal.en: Ankles is the regular plural, with no doubling.
normal.cn: 复数 ankles 规则变化，不双写字母。

normal.en: Ankle socks stop right at the ankle.
normal.cn: ankle socks 正好停在脚踝处。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-kle.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AN-kle。

abstract.en: See the bone that stands out at the side of the foot.
abstract.cn: 想象脚外侧突出的那块骨。

abstract.en: Hear a sharp gasp after a bad step.
abstract.cn: 听到踩空后一声急促的抽气。

abstract.en: Feel ice under a thin sock.
abstract.cn: 感到薄袜下冰凉的台阶。

examples.en: He broke his ankle playing football.
examples.cn: 他踢球时摔断了脚踝。

examples.en: Her ankle was still swollen a week later.
examples.cn: 一周后她的脚踝仍然肿着。

examples.en: The path was ankle-deep in mud.
examples.cn: 小路上的泥没过了脚踝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 与 angle（角、弯折）同源：腿在脚上方弯折的那个关节，脚踝。

root: 来自古英语 anclēow，上溯原始日耳曼语 ankulaz，词根义为「弯折、弯曲」，与 angle（角）同源；指腿在脚上方弯折处的关节。

sensesIntro.en: One sense is the joint; the other measures how high something reaches on the leg.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项指关节本身，另一个义项量度某物在腿上达到的高度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the bone that stands out above the heel.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚跟上方突出的骨节。

branches.en: a twisted ankle
branches.cn: 扭伤的脚踝

branches.en: a broken ankle
branches.cn: 骨折的脚踝

branches.en: ankle-deep water
branches.cn: 没到脚踝的水

branches.en: ankle socks
branches.cn: 踝袜

branches.en: ankle boots
branches.cn: 短靴

intro.en: A short native noun that forms compounds freely with clothing and depth words.
intro.cn: 这是一个简短的本族名词，容易与衣物、深度类词构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Germanic; the Latin cognate angulus appears only in the related word angle.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是日耳曼语；拉丁同源词 angulus 只出现在相关的 angle 中。

items.meaning: an ornament worn at the ankle

definition_zh: 可行的；可能实现的；合理的
definition_en: possible to do or carry out, likely to succeed, or reasonable to believe
core_image: 桌上摊着预算表和草图，几个人正拿笔圈出还能省下的几项开支
scene: 他们把预算算了一遍，发现这个方案确实能做成。 The plan looked feasible after the cost check.
sceneCN: 这里 feasible 是「可行的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：经过成本核算，这个方案看起来可行。

senses.title: Possible to do
senses.definition: able to be done or carried out with the resources available
senses.definitionCN: 用现有资源能够完成或实施
senses.example: The plan is technically feasible.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案在技术上是可行的。
senses.why: This is the main sense in planning and engineering.
senses.whyCN: 这是计划与工程语境中的主要含义。

senses.title: Likely to succeed
senses.definition: likely to work or succeed in practice
senses.definitionCN: 在实践中很可能奏效或成功
senses.example: It is not feasible to finish today.
senses.exampleCN: 今天完工是不现实的。
senses.why: Feasible often adds a judgment about success.
senses.whyCN: feasible 常带有对成功可能性的判断。

senses.title: Reasonable to believe
senses.definition: reasonable or plausible as an explanation
senses.definitionCN: 作为解释显得合理或可信
senses.example: That is a feasible explanation for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 这是对延误的一种合理解释。
senses.why: The sense extends from actions to ideas that can stand up.
senses.whyCN: 该义从行动延伸到站得住脚的想法。

intro.en: Feasible comes from Old French faisable, from Latin facere, to do or make.
intro.cn: feasible 源自古法语 faisable，最终出自拉丁语 facere（做、制作）。

items.en: Facere meant to do or make.
items.cn: facere 意为做或制作。

items.en: Faisable meant able to be done.
items.cn: faisable 意为能够做到的。

items.en: Feasible entered English with the sense of practicable.
items.cn: feasible 以「可实行的」之义进入英语。

items.en: The word spread into planning and engineering.
items.cn: 该词扩展到规划与工程领域。

items.en: Feasible now also describes reasonable explanations.
items.cn: 现代英语中 feasible 也形容合理的解释。

note.en: Feasible is compared with similar-looking words and with words for what can be done.
note.cn: 把 feasible 与形近词以及表示「可做到」的词作比较。

entries.definition: able to bend or change easily
able to be seen
showing good judgment
able to happen or be done
useful and likely to work
able to operate successfully

normalIntro.en: Feasible asks whether something can really be done, not just imagined.
normalIntro.cn: feasible 追问某事是否真能做出来，而不只是想象。

normal.en: Feasible shares a root with factory and fact.
normal.cn: feasible 与 factory、fact 共享同一个词根。

normal.en: A feasibility study tests whether a plan can work.
normal.cn: 可行性研究检验计划能否成立。

normal.en: Technically feasible means the science allows it.
normal.cn: technically feasible 指技术上允许做到。

normal.en: Economically feasible means the money also works.
normal.cn: economically feasible 指经济上也划算。

normal.en: Infeasible adds in- to mean not doable.
normal.cn: infeasible 加 in- 表示不可行。

abstract.en: A dream becomes a plan when it becomes feasible.
abstract.cn: 梦想变得可行时才成为计划。

abstract.en: Feasibility is a conversation between ambition and resources.
abstract.cn: 可行性是雄心与资源之间的一场对话。

abstract.en: What is possible is not always what is wise.
abstract.cn: 可能做到的事并不总是明智之事。

examples.en: The plan is technically feasible.
examples.cn: 这个方案在技术上是可行的。

examples.en: It is not feasible to finish today.
examples.cn: 今天完工是不现实的。

examples.en: Engineers proposed a feasible solution.
examples.cn: 工程师提出了一个可行的解决方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: feasible 与 fact、factory 同源，都来自拉丁语 facere（做），字面是「能够被做出来的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 facere（做、制作），经古法语 faisable，核心义「能够做成的」。

sensesIntro.en: Feasible means possible to do, likely to succeed, or reasonable as an explanation.
sensesIntro.cn: feasible 意为可以做、很可能成功，或作为解释显得合理。

core.en: Something that can be carried out with real means.
core.cn: 用现实手段能够实施的事物。

branches.en: A task that can actually be done.
branches.cn: 真正能够完成的任务。

branches.en: A plan likely to succeed.
branches.cn: 很可能成功的计划。

branches.en: An idea that can be reasonably believed.
branches.cn: 可以合理相信的想法。

branches.en: Being doable and being likely to work often overlap.
branches.cn: 「做得到」与「容易成功」常常重叠。

branches.en: A workable plan and a plausible story both hold together.
branches.cn: 可行的计划与可信的说法都自洽。

intro.en: Feasible builds words for possibility, practicality, and their opposites.
intro.cn: feasible 构成表示可能性、实际性及其反面的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere and facilis lie behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere 与 facilis 是该词的词源基础。

items.exampleCN: 他们完成了可行性研究。

items.example: It could feasibly be done by June.
items.exampleCN: 这件事在六月前完成是可行的。
这个进度表被证明不可行。

items.example: The route was unfeasible in winter.
items.exampleCN: 这条路线在冬天难以实行。

items.example: The committee questioned the feasibleness of the idea.
items.exampleCN: 委员会质疑这个想法的可行性。

items.meaning: easy to do or too simple
items.exampleCN: 他给了一个肤浅的回答。

items.meaning: ease or a place built for a purpose

definition_zh: 通信；信件往来；一致；对应
definition_en: letters exchanged between people, or a close similarity between two things
core_image: 一只木盒里叠着几十封来回旅行的信
scene: 两个笔友从中学写到工作，抽屉里塞满了对方的来信。 Their correspondence lasted more than twenty years.
sceneCN: 这里 correspondence 指「通信」（第 1 个义项：长期的书信往来）；句意是他们的通信持续了二十多年。

pos.zh: 通信；信件往来；一致；对应

senses.title: Letters going both ways
senses.definition: the writing and receiving of letters between people
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间写信与收信的活动
senses.example: Their correspondence lasted more than twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的通信持续了二十多年。
senses.why: Two pens answer each other across a long silence.
senses.whyCN: 两支笔隔着漫长的沉默互相回答。

senses.title: A close agreement
senses.definition: a strong similarity between two accounts or sets of facts
senses.definitionCN: 两种说法或两组事实之间的高度相似
senses.example: There is a close correspondence between the two reports.
senses.exampleCN: 这两份报告高度一致。
senses.why: Two maps of one valley should agree on every bend.
senses.whyCN: 同一山谷的两张地图，应该在每个弯道处一致。

senses.title: A one-to-one link
senses.definition: a direct relationship in which each item on one side matches an item on the other
senses.definitionCN: 一方每一项都与另一方某一项相匹配的直接关系
senses.example: The chart shows the correspondence between sounds and symbols.
senses.exampleCN: 这张表显示了声音与符号之间的对应关系。
senses.why: Every key needs its own lock, and every sign its own meaning.
senses.whyCN: 每把钥匙都要有自己的锁，每个符号都要有自己的意思。

intro.en: Correspondence comes from Latin correspondere, to answer one another, from com-, together, and respondere, to answer.
intro.cn: correspondence 来自拉丁语 correspondere（彼此应答），由 com-（一起）与 respondere（回答）构成。

items.en: Respondere meant to answer or give a promise back.
items.cn: respondere 意为回答或回以承诺。

items.en: Correspondere meant to answer each other in turn.
items.cn: correspondere 意为彼此轮流应答。

items.en: Old French kept the word for an exchange of answers.
items.cn: 古法语保留了这个词，指回答的往来。

items.en: English correspondence named the exchange of letters.
items.cn: 英语 correspondence 指书信的往来。

items.en: It also names any tight fit between two sets of things.
items.cn: 它也表示两组事物之间严密的吻合。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the answering base respond-, and the meaning group names other words for letters and agreement.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示回答的词基 respond-，近义组列出其他表示书信与一致的说法。

entries.definition: to match or exchange letters
a reporter or a person who writes letters
matching in position or meaning
written messages sent by post
entries.definitionCN: 通过邮局寄出的书面信息

entries.definition: the state of having the same view
a thing that fits or equals another

normal.en: Two people keep up a correspondence; two facts show correspondence.

normal.en: A correspondence course travels by post instead of by bus.
normal.cn: 函授课程靠邮路而不是靠公交车来上课。

abstract.cn: 想象两支笔隔着多年，蘸进同一只墨水瓶。

abstract.en: Picture two maps with every river drawn in the same place.
abstract.cn: 想象两张地图把每条河都画在同一个位置。

abstract.en: Picture a row of keys facing a row of locks.
abstract.cn: 想象一排钥匙正对着一排锁。

examples.en: Their correspondence lasted more than twenty years.
examples.cn: 他们的通信持续了二十多年。

examples.en: There is a close correspondence between the two reports.
examples.cn: 这两份报告高度一致。

examples.en: She keeps her business correspondence in a grey box.
examples.cn: 她把商业信函放在一只灰色的盒子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 correspondence 记成 correspond（互相回应）加 ence：彼此回应的东西，就是通信与一致。

root: 源自拉丁语 correspondere（彼此应答），由 com-（一起）与 respondere（回答）构成，本指互相回应，后指书信往来与彼此一致。

sensesIntro.en: From letters answering each other, to reports that agree, and at last to signs paired with meanings.
sensesIntro.cn: 从彼此回应的书信，到互相一致的报告，最后到符号与意义的成对关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden box packed with letters that travelled both ways.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只木盒塞满来回旅行过的信。

branches.en: Two writers keep answering across the distance.
branches.cn: 两位写信人隔着距离不断回应。

branches.en: Two accounts of one event fit without a gap.
branches.cn: 同一事件的两种说法严丝合缝。

branches.en: Each sign on one side faces one sign on the other.
branches.cn: 一边的每个符号都对着另一边的某个符号。

branches.en: Letters and reports both aim at a meeting of two sides.
branches.cn: 书信与报告都指向两方的会合。

branches.en: Agreement in meaning and pairing in form are cousins.
branches.cn: 意思上的一致与形式上的配对是近亲。

intro.en: Correspondence is correspond plus the noun ending -ence, from Latin respondere, to answer.
intro.cn: correspondence 由 correspond 加名词词尾 -ence 构成，源于拉丁语 respondere（回答）。

latinIntro.en: The answering base spons- also runs through response, responsible and sponsor.
latinIntro.cn: 表示回答与承诺的词基 spons- 也贯穿 response、responsible 与 sponsor。

items.meaning: an exchange of answers or letters

items.example: He is responsible for the file.

definition_zh: 紧紧地；牢牢地；严密地；严格地
definition_en: in a firm, close, or strictly controlled way, so that nothing is loose or gaps remain
core_image: 十指扣住栏杆，指节发白，手一点也不松
scene: 山风把帐篷吹得呼呼作响，绳子得再拉一遍。 The ropes were pulled tightly across the pegs before the storm arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 tightly 是「紧紧地」（第 1 个义项：牢固、不松动）；句意为暴风雨来之前，绳子被紧紧拉过地钉。画面里有帐篷、地钉与绷直的绳。

pos.zh: 副词：紧紧地、牢牢地；严密地、严格地

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ly 的原形容词，义为「紧的、绷紧的」
由形容词加 -en 构成，义为「收紧；使变紧」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「紧；紧密程度」

senses.title: In a firm, close grip
senses.definition: with a firm hold that does not slip or loosen
senses.definitionCN: 以不会滑动或松开的牢固握持
senses.example: She held her hat tightly as the wind rose.
senses.exampleCN: 风起时她紧紧抓住帽子。
senses.why: The suffix -ly turns the adjective into a description of how an action is done, keeping the whole force of no slack.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成「动作如何进行」的描述，同时保留了「无余量」的全部力度。

senses.title: So as to leave no gap
senses.definition: in a way that closes or seals something completely
senses.definitionCN: 把某物完全闭合或封住
senses.example: The windows were shut tightly against the dust.
senses.exampleCN: 窗户被严严实实地关上挡尘土。
senses.why: A closure that leaves no gap is the adverb form of the packed image.
senses.whyCN: 不缝隙的闭合，是「挤紧」意象的副词形式。

senses.title: In a packed or crowded way
senses.definition: so that things are pressed close together with little space
senses.definitionCN: 物件被挤得很近、几乎不留空间
senses.example: The passengers were tightly packed into the last bus.
senses.exampleCN: 乘客们被塞在末班车里，挤得满满当当。
senses.why: When things are packed with no room to move, the packing is described with this adverb.
senses.whyCN: 物件被挤得无从移动时，就用这个副词描述这种堆法。

senses.title: Under strict control
senses.definition: with strict rules, limits, or supervision
senses.definitionCN: 以严格的规则、限制或监督
senses.example: The chemical plant is tightly regulated.
senses.exampleCN: 这家化工厂受到严格监管。
senses.why: Rules with no looseness are described with the same adverb used for ropes.
senses.whyCN: 没有松懈的规矩，用与绳子同一个副词来描述。

senses.title: In a closely linked way
senses.definition: in a way that keeps people or things closely connected
senses.definitionCN: 使人或事物保持紧密联系的方式
senses.example: The small village is tightly knit around its fishing fleet.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小村庄围绕渔船队紧密相连。
senses.why: People bound as firmly as knotted rope are said to be tightly linked.
senses.whyCN: 像打结的绳一样绑紧的人们被称为紧密相连。

senses.title: With little time to spare
senses.definition: with very little space between events or deadlines
senses.definitionCN: 事件或期限之间几乎没有空档
senses.example: The two meetings were tightly scheduled back to back.
senses.exampleCN: 两场会议紧挨着排得满满当当。
senses.why: Hours packed without slack are described by the adverb of packing.
senses.whyCN: 小时被挤得没有空隙，就用「挤」的副词来描述。

senses.title: In a narrow, close result
senses.definition: in a way that shows only a small difference between sides
senses.definitionCN: 显示双方差距很小的方式
senses.example: The vote was tightly contested until the last district reported.
senses.exampleCN: 直到最后一个选区报出结果，这场投票都争夺得很接近。
senses.why: Two sides held close together hardly separate, and the adverb carries that closeness into the contest.
senses.whyCN: 双方贴近得几乎分不开，这个副词把这种贴近带进竞争里。

senses.title: With narrowed, narrowed eyes
senses.definition: used of eyes squeezed nearly shut
senses.definitionCN: 形容眼睛几乎闭合
senses.example: He listened with his eyes tightly shut.
senses.exampleCN: 他闭紧眼睛听。
senses.why: The same closing with no gap applies to eyelids, which also shut without slack.
senses.whyCN: 同样「合得无缝」也适用于眼睑，眼睑也能严丝合缝地闭上。

intro.en: The adverb is the adjective tight with the native suffix -ly, so its history follows the adjective once the ending is set.
intro.cn: 这个副词是形容词 tight 加本土后缀 -ly，所以结尾确定后，其历史就随形容词走。

items.en: The root thight already described what is dense and closely packed.
items.cn: 词根 thight 已用来形容密集、挤紧之物。

items.en: The adjective settles into the sense of firmly fixed, and adverbial use appears.
items.cn: 形容词定型为「固定牢靠」，副词用法随之出现。

items.en: The suffix -ly, from the Old English adjective ending -lic, becomes the regular adverb maker.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 源自中古英语形容词词尾 -lic，成为常规的副词构成手段。

items.en: Tightly spreads to packed crowds, strict rules, and close schedules.
items.cn: tightly 扩展到拥挤人群、严格规则与紧凑日程。

items.en: Technical and official writing favours tightly controlled and tightly packed.
items.cn: 技术与官方写作常用 tightly controlled 与 tightly packed。

items.en: The adverb is now fully regular and has no separate lexical history.
items.cn: 这个副词如今完全规则化，没有独立的词义史。

note.en: The look-alikes are the adjective family behind the adverb, and the near-meaning group offers other adverbs of firmness.
note.cn: 形近组是其后的形容词词族，近义组给出其它表示牢固的副词。

entries.definition: firmly stretched or closely fitting
to make or become tight
the quality of being tight
closely connected as a group
entries.definitionCN: 紧密团结的；复合词形式

entries.definition: in a solid and steady way
in a way that is safe from slipping or loss
with little space or distance between
in a slack or relaxed way

normalIntro.en: These memories go through the adjective behind the adverb, its suffix, and its frequent partners.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条通过副词背后的形容词、它的后缀与常见搭配来记。

normal.en: Tightly is tight plus -ly, so learn the adjective and the adverb follows.
normal.cn: tightly 是 tight 加 -ly，记住形容词，副词自然跟上。

normal.en: Hold tightly is the most natural partner: grip the verb and the adverb together.
normal.cn: hold tightly 是最自然的搭配：把动词和副词一起记。

normal.en: Tightly packed is the crowds-and-cargo phrase of the word.
normal.cn: tightly packed 是这个词用于人群与货物的短语。

normal.en: Tightly controlled shows the same adverb serving rules rather than ropes.
normal.cn: tightly controlled 显示同一个副词也能用于规则而非绳子。

normal.en: The adverb never becomes tightlier; only the adjective takes -er and -est.
normal.cn: 这个副词不能写成 tightlier，只有形容词才有比较级和最高级。

abstract.en: Picture a sailor's hands pulling a rope until the veins stand up.
abstract.cn: 想象水手把绳子拉到青筋凸起。

abstract.en: Think of a jam jar closed by someone stronger than you, and the lid will not turn.
abstract.cn: 想一只被人用力拧紧的果酱罐，盖子纹丝不动。

abstract.en: A tightly knit village is a net whose knots sit close together.
abstract.cn: 紧密团结的村庄就是一张结子挨得很近的网。

examples.en: He held the railing tightly as the ship rolled.
examples.cn: 船身摇晃时他死死抓住栏杆。

examples.en: The box was tightly packed with old letters.
examples.cn: 箱子里塞满了旧信件。

examples.en: Her eyes were tightly closed against the bright sun.
examples.cn: 她的眼睛紧紧闭着，躲避刺眼的阳光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太特利」——绳子捆得太特别利索，一点缝都没留。

root: 由形容词 tight（古英语 thight，密集的）加本土副词后缀 -ly 构成，词义史随形容词，无独立来源。

sensesIntro.en: Every use of the adverb is one shade of the same picture: no slack, whether in grip, closure, packing, rules, schedules, results, or closed eyes.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词的每种用法都是同一幅图的一种色调：无论握持、闭合、堆积、规则、日程、结果还是闭眼，都是「没有余量」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grip or a closure with zero slack anywhere.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次握持或一次闭合，处处没有余量。

branches.en: Firm holding and complete closing of the body.
branches.cn: 牢固握持与身体的完全闭合。

branches.en: Sealing a space against outside air or dust.
branches.cn: 把空间对外界封住。

branches.en: Packing in space and in time.
branches.cn: 在空间与时间上的挤满。

branches.en: Strict control and close human bonds.
branches.cn: 严格控制与紧密的人间纽带。

branches.en: A contest with almost no gap between sides.
branches.cn: 双方几乎没有差距的竞争。

intro.en: The affix work here is the productive -ly ending, which is added to an adjective that already carries the whole meaning.
intro.cn: 这里的构词要点是能产的 -ly 结尾，它加在一个已承载全部意义的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: Tightly has no Latin etymon; the borrowed Latin items below are offered only as semantic parallels.
latinIntro.cn: tightly 没有拉丁词源；下面借入的拉丁词仅作语义对照。

items.example: The whole meaning belongs to this base.
items.exampleCN: 全部意义都落在这个词基上。

items.example: It marks tightly as an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它使 tightly 成为副词。

items.example: The ending was itself once an adjective form.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾本身也曾经是形容词形式。

items.example: The adjective, not the adverb, takes it.
items.exampleCN: 只有形容词可用，副词不可。

definition_en: a small shallow dish on which a cup is placed
core_image: 早餐桌上，一只茶杯稳稳放在小圆碟上
scene: 早餐桌上，茶杯稳稳放在小碟上。 The cup rests on a saucer.
sceneCN: 这里 saucer 是「茶托」（第 1 个义项）；句意：茶杯稳稳地放在茶托上。

collocations.phrase: place the cup on the saucer

senses.title: Dish under a cup
senses.definition: a small shallow dish on which a cup is placed
senses.definitionCN: 用来垫放茶杯的小浅碟
senses.example: She set the teacup back on its saucer.
senses.exampleCN: 她把茶杯放回茶托上。
senses.why: The core sense is the small plate that catches drips from a cup.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是承接杯中滴液的小碟子。

senses.title: Small shallow dish
senses.definition: any small shallow round dish used for serving
senses.definitionCN: 任何用于盛放食物的小浅圆盘
senses.example: The cat drank milk from a saucer.
senses.exampleCN: 猫从浅碟里喝牛奶。
senses.why: The cup dish extends to other small round dishes.
senses.whyCN: 垫杯的小碟扩展为其他小圆盘。

senses.title: Flying saucer
senses.definition: a disc-shaped object reported in the sky, in the phrase flying saucer
senses.definitionCN: 短语 flying saucer 中指天空中出现的碟状飞行物
senses.example: The boy said he saw a flying saucer.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩说他看见了一个飞碟。
senses.why: The round shape links a tea dish to a disc in the sky.
senses.whyCN: 圆盘形状把茶碟与天空中的碟状物联系起来。

intro.en: Saucer first meant a sauce dish, then shifted to the dish under a cup.
intro.cn: saucer 最初指盛酱汁的碟子，后来转指垫茶杯的小碟。

items.en: Salsus, salted, is the distant root shared with sauce.
items.cn: salsus（盐腌的）是与 sauce 共有的远源。

items.en: Sauciere named a vessel for serving sauce.
items.cn: sauciere 指盛放酱汁的器皿。

items.en: Saucer entered English as a small sauce dish.
items.cn: saucer 以「小酱碟」之义进入英语。

items.en: The word shifted to the shallow dish under a cup.
items.cn: 该词转指垫在茶杯下的浅碟。

items.en: Flying saucer extended the round shape to the sky.
items.cn: flying saucer 把圆盘形状引申到天空。

note.en: Saucer is compared with similar spellings and with other tableware.
note.cn: 把 saucer 与形近拼写和其他餐具作比较。

normalIntro.en: Saucer is sauce plus -er, once a dish for sauce.
normalIntro.cn: saucer 是 sauce 加 -er，原本指盛酱汁的碟子。

normal.en: A saucer is the small dish that catches sauce drips.
normal.cn: saucer 是接住酱汁滴落的小碟子。

normal.en: The spelling keeps sauce and adds er at the end.
normal.cn: 拼写保留 sauce，并在末尾加上 er。

normal.en: Cup and saucer always appear as a pair on the table.

normal.en: A flying saucer is a round object, like a tea dish.

normal.en: Remember the phrase a saucer of milk for the cat.
normal.cn: 记住 a saucer of milk 这个给猫喝奶的搭配。

abstract.en: The saucer holds what the cup cannot keep.
abstract.cn: 茶托接住杯子留不住的东西。

abstract.en: A small dish can carry a large meaning in a tea ritual.
abstract.cn: 一只小碟在茶礼中承载着不小的意义。

abstract.en: The same round shape travels from table to sky.
abstract.cn: 同样的圆盘形状从餐桌走向天空。

examples.en: He placed the cup gently on the saucer.

examples.en: The saucer was cracked along one edge.
examples.cn: 茶碟的一边裂了。

examples.en: Children drew a flying saucer above the town.
examples.cn: 孩子们在小镇上空画了一个飞碟。

dict_mnemonic.text: saucer 由 sauce 加 -er 构成，原是盛酱汁的小碟，后来专指茶杯下的茶托。

sensesIntro.en: Saucer means the small dish under a cup, a shallow serving dish, or a flying disc.
sensesIntro.cn: saucer 意为茶杯下的小碟、盛食物的浅碟，或飞碟。

core.en: A small shallow dish linked to cups and sauce.
core.cn: 与茶杯和酱汁相关的小浅碟。

definition_zh: 忽略；未注意；俯瞰；宽容；监督
definition_en: to fail to notice something, to have a view over a place from above, to forgive a fault, or in older use to watch over work or people
core_image: 山腰旅店朝西的窗，窗下是一片屋瓦和几条窄巷
scene: 山腰的旅店有一扇朝西的窗，窗下是一片屋瓦和几条窄巷。 From the terrace you can overlook the whole harbour.
sceneCN: 这里 overlook 是「俯瞰」（第 2 个义项：从高处望下去）；句意为从平台上可以把整个港口尽收眼底，画面是那扇朝西的窗与窗下的屋瓦。

pos.zh: 忽略；未注意；俯瞰；宽容；监督

derivatives.zh: 由 overlook 加过去分词词尾 -ed 构成，义为「被忽略的」
由 overlook 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「监工；监督者」，多见于旧时纺织业记载

senses.title: To fail to notice something
senses.definition: to fail to see or consider something important, usually without intending to
senses.definitionCN: 没能看到或考虑到重要的事，通常并非有意
senses.example: The report overlooks one important detail.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告漏掉了一个重要细节。
senses.why: The verb pictures an eye sweeping over a surface; whatever the sweep passes across without stopping is literally looked over, and that is the root of the modern sense of missing it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词画的是目光扫过一整片表面；凡是目光扫过却没有停下的地方，就是字面地被「看过而越过」，现代「漏看」义正由此而来。

senses.title: To have a view over a place from above
senses.definition: to be built or placed high enough to give a view down onto a place
senses.definitionCN: 建得或放得足够高，可以从上面望见某处
senses.example: Her office overlooks the river.
senses.exampleCN: 她的办公室可以俯瞰那条河。
senses.why: Here the eye really does travel over the whole scene from a height, so the word keeps its oldest physical meaning instead of turning it into a mistake.
senses.whyCN: 这里目光确实从高处扫过整片景物，所以这个词保留着最古老的身体经验，没有把它变成一种过失。

senses.title: To forgive a fault
senses.definition: to choose not to punish or complain about a fault, as if deciding not to see it
senses.definitionCN: 选择不处罚、不追究某个过失，好像决定不去看它
senses.example: The manager decided to overlook the late arrival.
senses.exampleCN: 经理决定不计较那次迟到。
senses.why: Forgiving is pictured as letting the eye pass over a fault without stopping on it; the same sweep that causes a genuine miss becomes, by choice, an act of leniency.
senses.whyCN: 宽恕被画成让目光从过失上滑过、不停留；同一次「扫过」，无意时是漏看，存心时就成了宽待。

senses.title: To watch over work or people
senses.definition: in older use, to keep an eye on workers or a process and make sure things are done properly
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的用法里指盯着工人或某道工序，确保事情做得妥当
senses.example: An old woman overlooked the girls at their sewing.
senses.exampleCN: 一位老妇人照看着这些姑娘做针线。
senses.why: A person standing above a workshop sees every bench at once, so the word for a wide view also served for supervision before oversee took over that job.
senses.whyCN: 站在作坊高处的人能一眼看见每张工作台，所以表示「放眼望全」的词也承担过监督之职，后来这份差事才交给 oversee。

intro.en: Overlook is an English compound of over and look; its story is the double edge of a gaze that sweeps across everything and therefore may stop on nothing.
intro.cn: overlook 是 over 与 look 的英语复合词，它的来历是一道目光的两面：既扫过全部，也可能什么都不停留。

items.en: Over and look are both inherited Germanic words, so the compound was formed in English rather than borrowed from French or Latin.
items.cn: over 与 look 都是日耳曼语固有词，所以这个复合词形成于英语内部，并非借自法语或拉丁语。

items.en: The recorded verb oferlocian meant to look over something, with the eye passing across a whole surface.
items.cn: 有记录的动词 oferlocian 意为「看过某物」，目光扫过整片表面。

items.en: Middle English overlooken kept the wide view and also began to mean passing over a thing without stopping on it.
items.cn: 中古英语 overlooken 保留「放眼望过」，也开始表示从某物上掠过而不再停留。

items.en: Two seemingly opposite senses grew from the same sweep of the eye: watching over a place, and letting a fault go by.
items.cn: 两个看似相反的义项从同一次扫视里长出来：一个是看住一处地方，一个是把过失放过去。

items.en: Modern English keeps the view from above, the failure to notice and the mild forgiveness, while the supervising sense has grown rare.
items.cn: 现代英语保留从高处望下去、漏看与轻微宽容三个义项，监督义则已少见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers inflected forms and other words built with the same prefix; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of ignoring, of viewing and of forgiving.
note.cn: 形近组收各种屈折形式与同一前缀构成的其他词；近义组收表示忽略、观看与宽恕的动词。

entries.definition: The past form, also used as an adjective for something not noticed.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式，也作形容词指未被注意的。

entries.definition: The present participle, often used of a building with a view.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，常用于描述有景可望的建筑。

entries.definition: To supervise work or people and make sure it is done properly.
entries.definitionCN: 监督管理或人员，确保事情做得妥当。

entries.definition: A failure to notice something, or the act of supervising.
entries.definitionCN: 未注意到某事，或监督这件事本身。

entries.definition: To pay no attention to something on purpose.
To fail to give proper care or attention to something.
entries.definitionCN: 未能给予应有的照料或注意。

entries.definition: To stop being angry with someone for a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 因某个过失而不再生某人的气。

entries.definition: To look carefully over a whole area or scene.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细察看一整片区域或景象。

normalIntro.en: The word is over plus look, and its hooks return to a gaze that covers everything, to the height it needs, and to what it chooses not to see.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 over 加 look，记忆钩子都回到那道覆盖一切的目光、它需要的高度，以及它选择不看的东西。

normal.en: Overlook is over plus look, so the eye is pictured moving across a surface rather than fixing on a point.
normal.cn: overlook 是 over 加 look，画面里目光扫过一整片表面，而不是停在一点上。

normal.en: A building that overlooks the sea really does have that view, which is why the oldest sense survives unchanged.
normal.cn: 俯瞰大海的房子确实有那片景，所以最老的义项原样活了下来。

normal.en: The same sweep explains the mistake: what the eye passes over is not registered.
normal.cn: 同一次扫视也解释了过失：目光掠过的东西没有被记下。

normal.en: Forgiving adds a choice to the same picture, since the fault is deliberately allowed to pass.
normal.cn: 宽恕在同一幅画上加了选择：过失被故意放了过去。

normal.en: Oversee and oversight show that supervision once shared this prefix's wide view.
normal.cn: oversee 与 oversight 说明监督原本也共享这个前缀的「放眼望全」。

abstract.en: A window above a harbour with roofs and alleys below is the word as pure view.
abstract.cn: 港口上方的窗，下面是屋瓦与窄巷，就是这个词作为纯粹视野的样子。

abstract.en: A clerk running a finger down a list and skipping a line shows how a view becomes an error.
abstract.cn: 职员手指顺着名单下滑、跳过一行，显示视野如何变成错误。

abstract.en: A manager closing a file without a word turns the same skipped line into mercy.
abstract.cn: 经理一言不发合上卷宗，把同一行被跳过的地方变成了宽容。

examples.en: The report overlooks one important detail.
examples.cn: 这份报告漏掉了一个重要细节。

examples.en: Her office overlooks the river.
examples.cn: 她的办公室可以俯瞰那条河。

examples.en: The manager decided to overlook the late arrival.
examples.cn: 经理决定不计较那次迟到。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃路克」——欧沃站在高处往下看，看得远，也容易漏看。

root: overlook 由古英语 ofer（在上、越过）与 lōcian（看）合成，字面为「从上面看过去」；两半都是日耳曼语固有词，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a gaze sweeping across a whole scene; the senses split into seeing everything from above, missing one thing in the sweep, forgiving by choice, and the old duty of watching over work.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一道扫过整片景物的目光；义项分成从高处看见全部、扫视中漏掉一处、存心放过过失，以及旧时看管工作的职责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a west-facing window in a hillside inn, roofs and narrow alleys lying below it.
core.cn: 核心意象：山腰旅店朝西的窗，窗下摊着屋瓦与窄巷。

branches.en: a finger running down a list and skipping a line
branches.cn: 手指顺名单下滑、跳过一行

branches.en: a window above a harbour full of roofs
branches.cn: 港口上方看得见满片屋瓦的窗

branches.en: a manager quietly closing the file
branches.cn: 经理悄悄合上卷宗

branches.en: an old woman watching a row of sewing girls
branches.cn: 老妇人看着一排做针线的姑娘

branches.en: one skipped line, once an error and once a kindness
branches.cn: 同一行被跳过的地方，一次是错，一次是情

intro.en: The word sets the Old English prefix for over before the verb to look, and the same pieces recur in oversee, oversight and the inflected forms.
intro.cn: 这个词把古英语中表示「在上」的前缀放在动词「看」前面，同样的部件还出现在 oversee、oversight 与各屈折形式里。

latinIntro.en: This compound is native Germanic and has no Latin family of its own; Latin super is a distant relative of the prefix, not a member of this word's history.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词是日耳曼语固有词，本身没有拉丁词族；拉丁语 super 只是前缀的远亲，不属于这个词的来历。

definition_en: sweet food eaten at the end of a meal
core_image: 正餐的盘子被收走，一小碟冰淇淋放到桌上，勺子还冒着凉气
scene: 服务员收走主菜的盘子，又端来一小碟淋了果酱的布丁。 We had apple pie for dessert.
sceneCN: 这里 dessert 指「甜点」（第 1 个义项：正餐之后吃的甜食）；句意是我们吃了苹果派当甜点。

senses.title: Sweet food after a meal
senses.definition: sweet food served after the main part of a meal
senses.definitionCN: 正餐主要部分之后端上的甜食
senses.example: We had apple pie for dessert.
senses.exampleCN: 我们吃了苹果派当甜点。
senses.why: The meal ends, and the mouth asks for one last pleasant thing.
senses.whyCN: 一餐结束了，嘴还想再要一件让人愉快的东西。

senses.title: The sweet course itself
senses.definition: the course at the end of a formal dinner, served with its own dishes
senses.definitionCN: 正式宴席末端的一道，配有自己的餐具
senses.example: The dessert came with a small glass of sweet wine.
senses.exampleCN: 甜点环节配了一小杯甜酒。
senses.why: A course is not just food; it has its own plates and its own moment.
senses.whyCN: 一道菜不只是食物，它有自己的盘子和自己的时刻。

intro.en: Dessert comes from French desservir, to clear the table, built on des-, un-, and servir, to serve.
intro.cn: dessert 来自法语 desservir（撤去餐具），由 des-（去除）与 servir（上菜、服务）构成。

items.en: Desservir meant to remove what had been served.
items.cn: desservir 指把已经上过的东西撤走。

items.en: Dessert named what came after the clearing, the last sweet course.
items.cn: dessert 指撤桌之后端上来的东西，也就是最后那道甜食。

items.en: English borrowed dessert for the fruit and sweets ending a dinner.
items.cn: 英语借来 dessert，指结束一顿晚餐的水果与甜食。

items.en: Sugar and cheap ovens turned it into cakes and ices.
items.cn: 糖与便宜烤炉让它变成蛋糕和冰品。

items.en: The single s in the middle still separates it from a dry desert.
items.cn: 中间那个单独的 s，至今把它与干旱的沙漠分开。

note.en: The look-alike group is the famous one-s and two-s trap, and the meaning group gathers sweet endings to a meal.
note.cn: 形近组就是那个著名的一个 s 与两个 s 的陷阱，近义组则聚起一餐的甜味收尾。

entries.definition: a large area of dry sand
a spoon used for sweet dishes
as much as one dessertspoon holds
a sweet dish eaten after dinner
a cooked sweet dish
a baked sweet food made with flour

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a cleared dinner plate and end with the feeling of one last sweet bite.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从收空的餐盘开始，落到最后一口甜味的感觉。

normal.en: Two s for the sweet, one s for the sand.
normal.cn: 甜的那个有两个 s，沙的那个只有一个。

normal.en: Dessert is literally the food that arrives after the table is cleared.
normal.cn: dessert 字面上就是撤桌之后才到的那份食物。

normal.en: A desert has no water; a dessert needs no water at all.
normal.cn: 沙漠缺水，甜点则根本用不着水。

normal.en: The last course is the one the meal remembers.
normal.cn: 最后一道菜，往往是一顿饭记得最久的那道。

normal.en: Say the word slowly and the double s keeps the sweetness in.
normal.cn: 慢慢念这个词，那两个 s 把甜味留在了里面。

abstract.en: Picture a small dish set down where the main plate had been.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小碟放在原来主菜盘的位置上。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon lifting one cold, dark curl of chocolate.
abstract.cn: 想象一把匙舀起一小卷冰凉的深色巧克力。

abstract.en: Picture a candle still burning beside an empty coffee cup.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛还亮着，旁边是空掉的咖啡杯。

examples.en: We had apple pie for dessert.
examples.cn: 我们吃了苹果派当甜点。

examples.en: The dessert came with a small glass of sweet wine.
examples.cn: 甜点环节配了一小杯甜酒。

examples.en: She ordered two desserts because she could not choose.
examples.cn: 她点了两份甜点，因为实在选不出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dessert 记成「地舌特」：两个 s 像两勺糖，糖多的那个才是甜点。

root: 来自法语 desservir（撤去餐具），由 des-（去除）与 servir（上菜）构成。本义是撤桌之后端上来的东西，后来专指正餐末尾的甜食与甜点那一道，中间两个 s 的拼写也成了它与沙漠的区别。

sensesIntro.en: From the food brought after the plates are cleared, to the ritual course that ends a formal dinner.
sensesIntro.cn: 从撤盘之后端来的食物，到正式宴席末尾那一道仪式性的甜点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small sweet dish placed where the main plate was.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只小甜碟放在原来主菜盘的位置。

branches.en: The first sense is simply the sweet food at the end.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是结尾那份甜的食物。

branches.en: The second sense is that food raised into a formal course.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是这份食物被抬成正式的一道。

branches.en: Pie, ice and fruit all count as this closing sweetness.
branches.cn: 派、冰品与水果，都算作这种收尾的甜。

branches.en: Everyday dinners and state banquets both end on the same note.
branches.cn: 家常晚饭与国宴，都以同一个音收尾。

branches.en: A course brings its own spoon, its own plate and its own pause.
branches.cn: 一道菜自带它的匙、它的盘与它的停顿。

intro.en: Dessert forms a small family of dishes and spoons used at the sweet end of a meal.
intro.cn: dessert 长出一小族词，都与一餐甜味收尾时的餐具和食物有关。

latinIntro.en: The base is French servir, to serve, and des- means the serving is taken away again.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是法语 servir（上菜），前缀 des- 表示把上过的东西再撤走。

items.example: We had ice cream for dessert.
Use a dessertspoon for the pudding.
The dessert menu is on the wall.

items.meaning: a sweet wine served with dessert
items.example: They opened a bottle of dessert wine.

items.meaning: the sweet stage of a dinner
items.example: The dessert course lasted an hour.
items.exampleCN: 甜点环节持续了一个小时。

definition_en: the line where the sky meets the land or sea
core_image: 海上一条细线把天空和水面分开
scene: 太阳沉到了地平线以下。 The sun sank below the horizon.
sceneCN: 这里 horizon 是「地平线」（第 1 个义项）；句意：太阳沉到了地平线以下。

senses.title: Where sky meets earth
senses.definition: the line where the sky seems to meet the land or sea
senses.definitionCN: 天空看似与陆地或海面相接的那条线
senses.example: The sun sank below the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳沉到了地平线以下。
senses.why: This is the concrete visual sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是具体的视觉义项。

senses.title: The range of experience
senses.definition: the limit of what a person knows or has experienced
senses.definitionCN: 一个人知识与经历所及的范围
senses.example: Travel broadened her horizons.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行开阔了她的眼界。
senses.why: Here the line becomes a metaphor for knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 这里把那条线比喻为知识边界。

intro.en: Horizon comes from Greek horizein, to bound, through the idea of a bounding circle.
intro.cn: horizon 来自希腊语 horizein（界定），原指围绕大地的边界圆。

items.en: Horizein meant to bound or limit.
items.cn: horizein 意为界定、划界。

items.en: Horizon meant the bounding circle.
items.cn: horizon 意为界圈。

items.en: Horizon kept the astronomical sense.
items.cn: horizon 保留了天文学含义。

items.en: Orizon meant the line of the sky.
items.cn: orizon 意为天与地的分界线。

items.en: Horizon also meant the limit of knowledge.
items.cn: horizon 也指知识的边界。

note.en: Horizon is compared with look-alike words and with words for view and scope.
note.cn: 把 horizon 与形近词以及表示视野范围的词作比较。

entries.definition: flat and level
causing horror
a chemical in the body
the outline of things against the sky
a wide distant view
the range of something

normalIntro.en: The horizon is the line where the visible world ends and the sky begins.
normalIntro.cn: 地平线是可见世界的尽头与天空开始的地方。

normal.en: The sun sank below the horizon.
normal.cn: 太阳沉到了地平线以下。

normal.en: Travel broadened her horizons.
normal.cn: 旅行开阔了她的眼界。

normal.en: A ship appeared on the horizon.
normal.cn: 一艘船出现在地平线上。

normal.en: New horizons opened after graduation.
normal.cn: 毕业后新的天地展开了。

normal.en: The mountains stood along the distant horizon.
normal.cn: 群山沿着遥远的地平线矗立。

abstract.en: The horizon moves with every step we take.
abstract.cn: 地平线随着我们每一步而移动。

abstract.en: What lies beyond the horizon is not empty, only unseen.
abstract.cn: 地平线之外并非空无一物，只是看不见。

abstract.en: A wider horizon makes room for a wider self.
abstract.cn: 更宽的地平线，为更宽的自我留出空间。

examples.en: The sun sank below the horizon.
examples.cn: 太阳沉到了地平线以下。

examples.en: Travel broadened her horizons.
examples.cn: 旅行开阔了她的眼界。

examples.en: A ship appeared on the horizon.
examples.cn: 一艘船出现在地平线上。

dict_mnemonic.text: horizon 是「地平线」，引申为「眼界」；broaden horizons 是开阔眼界，on the horizon 表示在地平线上或即将到来。

root: 来自希腊语 horizein（界定），原指围绕大地的界圈，后指天地的分界线，又引申为知识与经历的边界。

sensesIntro.en: Horizon means the line where sky meets land, or the limit of a person's experience.
sensesIntro.cn: horizon 表示天与地相接的地平线，也可指个人经历与知识的边界。

core.en: The line where the known view ends.
core.cn: 已知视野结束的那条线。

branches.en: The sun sank below the horizon.
branches.cn: 太阳沉到了地平线以下。

branches.en: A ship appeared on the horizon.
branches.cn: 一艘船出现在地平线上。

branches.en: Travel broadened her horizons.
branches.cn: 旅行开阔了她的眼界。

branches.en: A line in the eye becomes a line in the mind.
branches.cn: 眼中的线，变成心中的边界。

branches.en: New horizons opened after graduation.
branches.cn: 毕业后新的天地展开了。

intro.en: Horizon builds horizontal and compounds such as event horizon.
intro.cn: horizon 可构成 horizontal，以及 event horizon 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Greek horizein, to bound.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根是希腊语 horizein，意为界定。

items.example: The sun set below the horizon.

items.exampleCN: 设计使用了醒目的水平线。

items.meaning: the boundary of a black hole
items.exampleCN: 任何东西都逃不出事件视界。

items.example: The ball moves on a horizontal plane.

latinEntries.example: Horizein is the source of horizon.
latinEntries.exampleCN: horizein 是 horizon 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Horizon entered Latin as a term of astronomy.
latinEntries.exampleCN: horizon 作为天文学术语进入拉丁语。

definition_en: the act of changing a text or studying again
core_image: 三稿叠在一起，最上面一版布满红色改线
scene: 交稿前，她把三稿叠在一起，完成最后一轮修订。 Before the deadline, she stacked the three drafts and finished the final revision.
sceneCN: 这里 revision 是「修订」（第 1 个义项：修改文字的行为）；句意：交稿前，她把三稿叠在一起，完成最后一轮修订。

senses.title: Changing a text
senses.definition: the act of changing writing to improve it
senses.definitionCN: 改动文字使其更好的行为
senses.example: The essay needs another revision.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章还需要再修订一次。
senses.why: Revision is the noun of revise, the act of looking again and changing.
senses.whyCN: revision 是 revise 的名词，指再看并改动的行为。

senses.title: A changed version
senses.definition: a version that has been changed
senses.definitionCN: 经过修改的版本
senses.example: The revision is much clearer than the draft.
senses.exampleCN: 修订版比初稿清楚得多。
senses.why: The act produces a new version, which also bears the name.
senses.whyCN: 这一行为产生新版本，新版本也叫 revision。

senses.title: Exam study
senses.definition: study done before an exam
senses.definitionCN: 考试前的学习
senses.example: He did two hours of revision each night.
senses.exampleCN: 他每晚复习两个小时。
senses.why: British English uses revision for the study that precedes an exam.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语用 revision 指考试前的复习。

intro.en: Revision comes from Latin revisio, a looking again, from revisere.
intro.cn: revision 源自拉丁语 revisio（再看），来自 revisere。

items.en: Revisere means to look at again.
items.cn: revisere 意为再看。

items.en: Revisio names the act of looking again.
items.cn: revisio 指再看的行为。

items.en: French revision keeps the act in its name.
items.cn: 法语 revision 在名称中保留了这一行为。

items.en: Revision first names the act of changing text.
items.cn: revision 最初指修改文字的行为。

items.en: British English adds exam study to the meaning.
items.cn: 英式英语又加入了考试复习的含义。

note.en: Revision is the noun; revisionism is a very different idea.
note.cn: revision 是名词；revisionism 指完全不同的历史修正主义。

entries.definition: to change and improve
changed and improved
a person who revises
a small change to a text
a published version of a book
the act of making something right

normalIntro.en: Revision is the second look that leaves red marks.
normalIntro.cn: revision 是留下红色批注的第二次审视。

normal.en: A major revision changes much of the text.
normal.cn: a major revision 改动大部分文字。

normal.en: A final revision is the last check.
normal.cn: a final revision 是最后一次检查。

normal.en: Revision notes help students study.
normal.cn: revision notes 帮助学生复习。

normal.en: The revision of a draft improves it.
normal.cn: 草稿的修订让它变得更好。

normal.en: Compare edition: an edition is printed, a revision is the change itself.
normal.cn: 对比 edition：edition 是印刷版本，revision 是改动本身。

abstract.en: Picture three stacks of paper with red lines across the top.
abstract.cn: 想象三叠纸，最上面一叠布满红线。

abstract.en: Imagine a sculptor cutting away stone for a second time.
abstract.cn: 想象雕塑家第二次凿去石料。

abstract.en: Think of a path being redrawn to reach the same place more easily.
abstract.cn: 想象重新画一条更容易到达同一地点的路。

examples.en: The plan is still under revision.
examples.cn: 计划仍在修订中。

examples.en: We made several revisions to the report.
examples.cn: 我们对报告做了几处修订。

examples.en: Her nightly revision paid off in the exam.
examples.cn: 她每晚的复习在考试中见效了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）＋ vision（看）」——再看一遍并动手改，就是修订。

root: 拉丁语 revisio（再看）→ 法语 revision → revision，核心义「再看并改动的行为及其成果」。

sensesIntro.en: Revision names the act of changing a text, then the changed version, and in British English the study before an exam.
sensesIntro.cn: revision 先指修改文字的行为，再指修改后的版本，英式英语中还指考试前的复习。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three stacked drafts covered in red marks.
core.cn: 核心意象：三叠布满红色批注的稿子。

branches.en: The act of changing text is the core.
branches.cn: 修改文字的行为是核心。

branches.en: A changed version also carries the name.
branches.cn: 修改后的版本也叫这个名字。

branches.en: British study before exams uses the word.
branches.cn: 英式英语用它指考前复习。

branches.en: The act and its result share one noun.
branches.cn: 行为与结果共用一个名词。

branches.en: Both changing text and exam study involve looking again.
branches.cn: 改文章与考前复习都包含再看一遍。

intro.en: Revision is revise plus the noun suffix -ion.
intro.cn: revision 是 revise 加名词后缀 -ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin revisio gives the word its shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 revisio 赋予这个词现在的形态。

latinEntries.example: Revisere leads to the noun revisio.

definition_zh: 警觉的；机敏的；警报；提醒；使警觉
definition_en: watchful and quick to notice things, a warning of danger, or to warn someone
core_image: 守夜人站在塔顶，耳朵转向黑暗里最轻的一声响
scene: 夜里仓库的灯忽然全亮了，值班的人抓起对讲机。 A security alert emptied the building within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 alert 是「警报」（第 2 个义项：提示危险、要求立即行动的警告）；句意为一条安全警报让整栋楼在几分钟内清空。图中可辨识物件：对讲机、应急灯、仓库门。

pos.zh: 动词：使警觉；提醒；向……报警

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「警觉地」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「警觉；机敏」
由 hyper- 加本词构成，义为「过度警觉的」

senses.title: Watchful and quick
senses.definition: paying close attention and ready to notice or react to something quickly
senses.definitionCN: 高度注意、能迅速察觉或反应的状态
senses.example: Drivers must stay alert on long night journeys.
senses.exampleCN: 长途夜间行车时司机必须保持警觉。
senses.why: The Italian source is a military lookout phrase, 'on the watch', so the adjective began as a description of a guard on duty.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的意大利语来源是军中的瞭望口令「处在警戒中」，所以形容词最初描述的是值班的哨兵。

senses.title: A warning of danger
senses.definition: a warning or announcement that danger or an emergency is present
senses.definitionCN: 告知危险或紧急情况存在的警告或通告
senses.example: A security alert emptied the building within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 一条安全警报让整栋楼在几分钟内清空。
senses.why: The lookout's shout became the message itself, so the noun names the warning rather than the watchman.
senses.whyCN: 哨兵的喊声变成了讯息本身，于是名词指的是那条警告，而不是守望的人。

senses.title: To warn someone
senses.definition: to warn someone about a danger or to make them aware of something urgent
senses.definitionCN: 就危险警告某人，或使其意识到紧急情况
senses.example: A neighbour alerted us to the smoke in the hallway.
senses.exampleCN: 一位邻居提醒我们走廊里有烟。
senses.why: The verb gives the warning a direction: the lookout's cry is now aimed at a particular person.
senses.whyCN: 动词给警告加上了方向：哨兵的喊声如今是对着某个具体的人发出的。

intro.en: Alert comes from an Italian military phrase meaning 'on the watch', and it still sounds like a sentry's word.
intro.cn: alert 来自一个意为「处在警戒中」的意大利军事短语，至今听起来仍像哨兵的用语。

items.en: All'erta meant 'on the height, on the watch', the position of a lookout on a tower.
items.cn: all'erta 意为「在高处、在警戒中」，指哨兵在塔上的位置。

items.en: French took the phrase as alerte, naming both the watch and the warning cry.
items.cn: 法语借作 alerte，既指警戒，也指警告的喊声。

items.en: English borrowed alerte first as a military order and soon as an adjective meaning watchful.
items.cn: 英语先借作军事口令，很快又用作表示「警觉的」形容词。

items.en: The noun widened to civilian warnings, from fire to weather, and the verb followed.
items.cn: 名词从军事扩展到民用的火警、天气等警告，动词随后出现。

items.en: Modern use ranges from a phone alert to a doctor's alertness, all from the same lookout post.
items.cn: 现代用法从手机警报一直到医生的警觉度，全都出自同一个瞭望岗位。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on alert; the near-meaning group gathers watchfulness and warnings.
note.cn: 形近组收由 alert 构成的词；近义组收警觉与警告类词。

entries.definition: The state of being watchful and quick to react.
In a watchful, attentive manner.
A warning device or the fear it causes.
entries.definitionCN: 警报装置，或它引起的恐惧。

entries.definition: Very careful to notice danger, especially over a long period.
entries.definitionCN: 长期保持警惕、留意危险的。

entries.definition: Attentive and looking out for possible trouble.
entries.definitionCN: 留心、注意可能出现的麻烦的。

entries.definition: A statement or sign that danger may be coming.
entries.definitionCN: 提示危险可能来临的话语或标志。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: the Italian phrase all'erta and its French reshaping alerte.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：意大利短语 all'erta 及其法语改写 alerte。

normal.en: Alert and alarm are cousins: one is the watch, the other the cry.
normal.cn: alert 与 alarm 是表亲：一个是守望，一个是呼喊。

normal.en: All'erta means 'on the height', so alert began as a position on a tower.
normal.cn: all'erta 意为「在高处」，所以 alert 最初是塔上的一个位置。

normal.en: Stay alert is an instruction to the eyes and ears, not to the feet.
normal.cn: stay alert 是对眼睛和耳朵下的指令，不是对脚。

normal.en: On alert is the state; an alert is the message; to alert is the action.
normal.cn: on alert 是状态，an alert 是讯息，to alert 是动作。

normal.en: One l, then e: a-l-e-r-t, not allert.
normal.cn: 一个 l 后接 e：a-l-e-r-t，不是 allert。

abstract.en: Alertness is a form of attention that assumes something may go wrong, which is why guards and editors both need it.
abstract.cn: 警觉是一种预设「可能出事」的注意力，所以哨兵与编辑都需要它。

abstract.en: The same word is a state, a message and an action, because a warning only exists across all three.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既是状态、又是讯息、又是动作，因为警告正是在这三者之间才成立。

abstract.en: A society that is permanently on alert eventually stops noticing the alerts.
abstract.cn: 长期处于警戒状态的社会，最终会不再注意那些警报。

examples.en: Drivers must stay alert on long night journeys.
examples.cn: 长途夜间行车时司机必须保持警觉。

examples.en: A security alert emptied the building within minutes.
examples.cn: 一条安全警报让整栋楼在几分钟内清空。

examples.en: A neighbour alerted us to the smoke in the hallway.
examples.cn: 一位邻居提醒我们走廊里有烟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，勒特」——额，勒特一听见动静就竖起耳朵，特别警觉。

root: 源自意大利语军事短语 all'erta「在高处、在警戒中」，经法语 alerte 进入英语，由「瞭望」引申为警觉、警报与报警。

sensesIntro.en: One lookout post produces all three senses: the guard's state, the cry he raises, and the act of raising it for someone else.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都出自同一个瞭望岗位：哨兵的状态、他发出的喊声，以及替别人发出喊声的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a watchman on a tower turns his ear towards the faintest sound in the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：塔上的守夜人把耳朵转向黑暗中那一声最轻的响动。

branches.en: a driver's eyes moving between mirror and road
branches.cn: 在后视镜与路面之间移动的司机目光

branches.en: a siren and a message on every phone
branches.cn: 响起的警报与每部手机上的通知

branches.en: a neighbour knocking hard on the door
branches.cn: 用力敲门的邻居

branches.en: a red light spinning above an entrance
branches.cn: 门口上方旋转的红灯

branches.en: one watchfulness, kept and passed on
branches.cn: 同一种警觉，自己保持，也传给别人

intro.en: An Italian phrase of place, its French form, and the English endings built on the borrowed word.
intro.cn: 一个表示位置的意大利短语、它的法语形式，以及建在这个借词上的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The phrase is Italian; erta goes back to Latin erectus, 'raised', so the list gives that Latin source.
latinIntro.cn: 这个短语属意大利语；erta 可追到拉丁语 erectus「竖起的」，因此列表给出这一拉丁来源。

items.meaning: on the height, on the watch

definition_en: a group of sheep or birds, a crowd of people, or to gather in large numbers
core_image: 一群羊挤成一团，沿山坡缓缓移动
scene: 一群羊在山坡上吃草。 A flock of sheep grazed on the hill.
sceneCN: 这里 flock 是「羊群」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一群羊在山坡上吃草。

senses.title: Group of sheep
senses.definition: a group of sheep or similar animals kept together
senses.definitionCN: 养在一起的一群羊或类似动物
senses.example: A flock of sheep grazed on the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 一群羊在山坡上吃草。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老也最具体的义项。

senses.title: Group of birds
senses.definition: a group of birds flying or feeding together
senses.definitionCN: 一起飞行或觅食的一群鸟
senses.example: A flock of geese crossed the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 一群大雁飞过天空。
senses.why: The word extends to other animals that stay together.
senses.whyCN: 这个词扩展到其他群居动物。

senses.title: Crowd
senses.definition: a large group of people, often moving together
senses.definitionCN: 一大群常常一起行动的人
senses.example: A flock of fans waited outside.
senses.exampleCN: 一大群粉丝在外面等候。
senses.why: People behaving like sheep are called a flock.
senses.whyCN: 像羊一样行动的人群被称作 flock。

senses.title: Gather
senses.definition: to move or gather in large numbers
senses.definitionCN: 大批地移动或聚集
senses.example: Tourists flock to the beach in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天游客涌向海滩。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb of crowding together.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为成群聚集的动词。

intro.en: Flock is an Old English word, flocc, meaning a group or troop.
intro.cn: flock 是古英语词 flocc，意为群体或队伍。

items.en: Flocc meant a group of people or animals.
items.cn: flocc 指一群人或动物。

items.en: The word was used for sheep and birds.
items.cn: 这个词用于羊群和鸟群。

items.en: Flock also named a Christian congregation.
items.cn: flock 也指基督教会的会众。

items.en: The verb meant to gather in numbers.
items.cn: 动词形式意为成群聚集。

items.en: Flock is used for crowds of people.
items.cn: flock 用于形容人群。

note.en: Flock is compared with similar-looking words and with words for groups of animals.
note.cn: 把 flock 与形近词以及表示动物群体的词作比较。

entries.definition: a solid piece
a device that shows time
to move with a quick motion
a group of cattle
a large group of people
a moving mass of insects

normalIntro.en: A flock is a group that moves as one: sheep, birds, or people drawn to the same place.
normalIntro.cn: flock 是作为一个整体移动的群体：羊、鸟，或被同一地方吸引的人。

normal.en: The flock moved down the hill.
normal.cn: 羊群向山下移动。

normal.en: Birds gathered in a large flock.
normal.cn: 鸟儿聚成一大群。

normal.en: Fans flocked to the concert.
normal.cn: 粉丝涌向音乐会。

normal.en: The shepherd counts his flock.
normal.cn: 牧羊人清点羊群。

normal.en: Sheep flock together for safety.
normal.cn: 羊群聚在一起以求安全。

abstract.en: A crowd can think like a flock.
abstract.cn: 人群的思维可以像羊群。

abstract.en: Following is easy inside a group.
abstract.cn: 在群体中跟随是容易的。

abstract.en: The shepherd knows the group by counting.
abstract.cn: 牧人通过计数来了解群体。

examples.en: A flock of sheep grazed on the hill.
examples.cn: 一群羊在山坡上吃草。

examples.en: A flock of geese crossed the sky.
examples.cn: 一群大雁飞过天空。

examples.en: Tourists flock to the beach in summer.
examples.cn: 夏天游客涌向海滩。

dict_mnemonic.text: flock 源自古英语 flocc（群体），核心义「聚成一群」，由羊群推及鸟群、人群与成群行动。

root: 源自古英语 flocc（群体、队伍），核心义「聚在一起的一群」。

sensesIntro.en: Flock means a group of sheep, birds, or people, or to gather in numbers.
sensesIntro.cn: flock 意为羊群、鸟群、人群，或成群聚集。

core.en: A group moving and staying together.
core.cn: 一起移动并待在一起的群体。

branches.en: Sheep kept and moved together.
branches.cn: 一起放养和移动的羊。

branches.en: Birds flying as one body.
branches.cn: 作为一个整体飞行的鸟。

branches.en: People gathered like animals.
branches.cn: 像动物一样聚拢的人。

branches.en: The act of crowding toward a place.
branches.cn: 成群涌向某处的动作。

branches.en: Animal groups and human crowds share the word.
branches.cn: 动物群与人群共用一个词。

intro.en: Flock builds a small family around groups and gathering.
intro.cn: flock 围绕群体与聚集构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Flock has no Latin ancestor; Latin grex, a herd, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flock 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 grex（群）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The lamb stayed near its flockmate.

items.meaning: a record of a sheep flock
items.exampleCN: 农场主保存羊群谱系册。

definition_en: to make practical use of something, especially in a way that puts it to good purpose
core_image: 把废木料锯开钉成一张结实的书架
scene: 院子里堆着装修拆下的旧木板，木匠量了量，决定把它们做成靠墙的架子。 They utilized every scrap of timber on the site.
sceneCN: 这里 utilize 是「利用」（第 1 个义项：把已有的东西拿来派上用场）；句意为他们把工地上每一块零碎木料都利用了起来。旧木料变成书架的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ation，义为「利用；使用」
同根名词，义为「效用；公用事业」
同根形容词，义为「实用的；功利的」
同义形容词，义为「可用的」

senses.title: To put something to practical use
senses.definition: to find a practical use for something that exists
senses.definitionCN: 为已有的东西找到实际用途
senses.example: The school utilized the old hall as a library.
senses.exampleCN: 学校把旧礼堂改作图书馆使用。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to use, and the suffix makes an English verb; together they add the idea of turning something to good account.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「使用」，后缀让它成为英语动词；合起来带上「把事情办得其所」的意味。

senses.title: To employ existing resources
senses.definition: to make efficient use of available supplies, money, or space
senses.definitionCN: 高效地使用现有的物资、资金或空间
senses.example: The team utilized the spare room for meetings.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把闲置的房间用来开会。
senses.why: Where supplies are limited, using them well became the point of the word, and efficiency lies in the background of this sense.
senses.whyCN: 物资有限时「把东西用得好」成了重点，这层意思背后始终有理性的计算。

senses.title: To adopt a method or skill
senses.definition: to adopt a technique or skill for a particular task
senses.definitionCN: 为某项任务采用一种技术或技能
senses.example: The hospital utilizes a new method of scanning.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院采用了一种新的扫描方法。
senses.why: Methods and skills are abstract tools, and anything that can be put to work fits the same frame.
senses.whyCN: 方法与技能是抽象的「工具」，凡能拿来干活的东西都套进同一个框架。

senses.title: In formal writing, simply to use
senses.definition: used in formal or technical writing simply where use would be plainer
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或技术性文字中替代更朴素的 use
senses.example: The report utilizes the term risk in two ways.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告以两种含义使用了风险一词。
senses.why: Formal style likes longer borrowed verbs, so the word often stands in for plain use without adding much.
senses.whyCN: 正式文体偏爱较长的借入动词，于是这个词常只当作 use 的替代，并未添多少新意。

intro.en: A formal English verb built in modern times from the Latin noun utilitas, useful.
intro.cn: 一个近代在英语中构造的正式动词，取自拉丁名词 utilitas（有用的）。

items.en: Uti meant to use, and utilis meant useful, with utilitas naming usefulness.
items.cn: uti 意为使用，utilis 意为有用的，utilitas 指有用性。

items.en: Utiliser appeared in French in the eighteenth century, built from the same Latin noun.
items.cn: utiliser 于十八世纪出现在法语中，同样由这个拉丁名词构造。

items.en: English forms utilize in the nineteenth century, following the French pattern.
items.cn: 英语循法语模式在十九世纪造出 utilize。

items.en: Technical writing takes it up at once for the efficient use of resources.
items.cn: 技术写作立刻采用它来表示资源的有效利用。

items.en: Modern style guides advise readers to prefer plain use where meaning is the same.
items.cn: 现代文风指南建议读者在意思相同时选用更朴素的 use。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the util- stem, and the near-meaning group separates plain use from efficient exploitation.
note.cn: 形近组共享 util- 词干，近义组则把朴素的 use 与高效的利用区分开。

entries.definition: usefulness or a public service
the act of putting to use
valued for being useful
to employ something
to use a method or tool
to use resources for gain
to put something into action
to fail to use something well

normalIntro.en: Read it as utility turned into a verb: to make the useful quality happen.
normalIntro.cn: 把它看成 utility 转成的动词：让「有用」这件事发生。

normal.en: The ending -ize marks it as a verb of making, like modernize and organize.
normal.cn: -ize 词尾标记这是「使……」类动词，如 modernize、organize。

normal.en: Utilize is formal; use is the everyday choice.
normal.cn: utilize 属正式用语，日常生活中用 use。

normal.en: Utilization is the noun, and it stays abstract.
normal.cn: 名词是 utilization，同样是抽象的。

normal.en: Widely utilized is a favourite passive phrase in reports.
normal.cn: widely utilized 是报告里最爱的被动说法。

normal.en: Utilize space and utilize resources are the two common objects.
normal.cn: 常见搭配对象是空间与资源。

abstract.en: Picture old planks cut and nailed into a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象旧木板被锯开、钉成一只书架。

abstract.en: See rain water caught in a barrel for the garden.
abstract.cn: 看雨水被接进桶里浇园子。

abstract.en: Hear a report say the empty hall is now in use, though it says utilize.
abstract.cn: 听报告说空礼堂现已投入使用，只是用了 utilize 这个词。

examples.en: The chef utilizes every part of the vegetable, down to the leaves.
examples.cn: 这位厨师把蔬菜的每一部分都利用起来，连叶子也不放过。

examples.en: Solar panels let the farm utilize its own roof space.
examples.cn: 太阳能板让农场利用起了自己的屋顶空间。

examples.en: The study utilizes data collected over ten years.
examples.cn: 这项研究运用了十年间收集的数据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优体来用」——好东西来了就用上，别搁着积灰。

root: 拉丁语 uti（使用）→ utilis（有用的）→ utilitas（有用性）；法语 utiliser 于十八世纪构造，英语十九世纪仿此造出 utilize

sensesIntro.en: A formal verb for putting things to use spreads to resources, to methods and skills, and to plain stylistic replacement for use.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个正式动词从「把东西用起来」扩展到资源、方法与技能，也成了 use 的文风替代品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scrap planks cut and nailed into a shelf.
core.cn: 核心意象：废木料被锯开、钉成书架。

branches.en: The use branch: something idle is given a job.
branches.cn: 使用分支：闲置之物被派上了活。

branches.en: The resource branch: supplies, money, and space used well.
branches.cn: 资源分支：物资、资金、空间被用好。

intro.en: The useful stem plus a verb ending of making: to make something useful in practice.

latinIntro.en: From Latin utilis, useful, built on uti, to use; the English verb ending -ize comes through French -iser.

scene: 炉子上的水壶正冒着热气。 The kettle on the stove is steaming.

definition_en: to officially join a course or organization, or to add someone's name to a list
core_image: 名字被写进一本厚厚的名册，从此成为其中一员
scene: 开学第一天，新生在体育馆前排起长队，把自己的名字写进课程名单。 She enrolled in two evening classes.
sceneCN: 这里 enroll 是「注册；报名」（第 1 个义项：正式加入课程或组织）；句意：她报名了两门晚间课程。

senses.title: To join officially
senses.definition: to put your name on an official list in order to join a course or group
senses.definitionCN: 把自己的名字登记在正式名单上，以加入课程或团体
senses.example: He enrolled in a French course at the college.
senses.exampleCN: 他在学院注册了一门法语课。
senses.why: The word is en- plus roll, a list, so enrolling is literally putting a name onto the roll.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 en- 加 roll（名册），所以 enroll 字面上就是把名字写进名册。

senses.title: To add someone to a list
senses.definition: to officially register another person as a member
senses.definitionCN: 正式把另一个人登记为成员
senses.example: The school enrolled forty new students this term.
senses.exampleCN: 学校这学期招收了四十名新生。
senses.why: The same list-making action is seen from the institution's side.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「造册」动作从机构的角度看，就是招收。

senses.title: To enlist for service
senses.definition: to join the armed forces, or to sign someone up for service
senses.definitionCN: 加入军队，或把某人登记入伍
senses.example: Thousands enrolled when the war began.
senses.exampleCN: 战争开始时，成千上万人应征入伍。
senses.why: Military service also keeps a roll of names, preserving the original list image.
senses.whyCN: 兵役同样保存名册，原初的「名单」画面得以保留。

intro.en: Enroll comes from Old French enroller, from en- plus rolle, a roll or list, ultimately Latin rotulus, a little wheel.
intro.cn: enroll 来自古法语 enroller，由 en- 加 rolle（卷轴、名册）构成，最终源于拉丁语 rotulus（小轮子）。

items.en: Rotulus means a little wheel or a rolled document.
items.cn: rotulus 意为小轮子或卷起来的文书。

items.en: Rolle means a roll of parchment, especially a list of names.
items.cn: rolle 指一卷羊皮纸，尤指名册。

items.en: Enroller means to put a name on a roll or register.
items.cn: enroller 意为把名字写入卷册或登记簿。

items.en: The verb enters English law with the sense of recording names officially.
items.cn: 这个动词进入英语法律，意为正式记录姓名。

items.en: Middle English enrollen covers membership, taxes, and military service.
items.cn: 中古英语 enrollen 涵盖成员登记、税册和兵役。

items.en: Modern English uses enroll mainly for schools, courses, and organizations.
items.cn: 现代英语中，enroll 主要用于学校、课程和组织。

note.en: Enroll is a roll-word, and it sits near verbs for registering, signing up, and enlisting.
note.cn: enroll 是一个「名册」词，与注册、报名和应征类动词相邻。

the act of enrolling or the number enrolled
a person who has enrolled
to put a name on an official list

normalIntro.en: Enroll contains roll, and a roll is a list of names, so enrolling is putting your name on that list.
normalIntro.cn: enroll 含有 roll，而 roll 指名册，所以 enroll 就是把名字写进名册。

normal.en: En- means put into, and roll means list: put your name into the list.
normal.cn: en- 表示放入，roll 表示名册：把名字放进名册。

normal.en: Enroll in is the pattern for joining a course.
normal.cn: enroll in 是加入课程的搭配。

normal.en: Enroll at a college marks the institution where the list is kept.
normal.cn: enroll at a college 标出名册所在的机构。

normal.en: The noun enrollment can mean the number of people on the list.
normal.cn: 名词 enrollment 可指名单上的人数。

normal.en: Compare enrol: British spelling drops one l.
normal.cn: 对比 enrol：英式拼写少一个 l。

abstract.en: Picture a long roll of paper unrolling across a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷长纸在桌上展开。

abstract.en: Imagine a pen writing your name at the bottom of a list.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔把你的名字写在名单末尾。

abstract.en: Think of a door where new members hand in a signed card.
abstract.cn: 想象新成员在门口交上签好的卡片。

examples.en: She enrolled in a photography class last month.
examples.cn: 她上个月报名了摄影课。

examples.en: The university enrolls students from many countries.
examples.cn: 这所大学招收来自许多国家的学生。

examples.en: He enrolled at the local college after finishing school.
examples.cn: 中学毕业后，他在当地学院注册入学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因肉」——把名字写进名单，从此有你的位置；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 rotulus（小轮、卷轴）→ 古法语 rolle（卷册、名册）→ enroller（写入名册）→ 中古英语 enrollen，指正式登记为成员。

sensesIntro.en: Putting your own name on the list comes first, then adding other names, then signing up for service.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是把自己的名字写进名单，再是把别人的名字加上，最后是登记服役。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name written onto a long roll and made official.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个名字被写进长名册，从此正式生效。

branches.en: Joining by adding your own name is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 通过写自己的名字加入，是基本义项。

branches.en: Adding someone else's name is the institution's side of the act.
branches.cn: 写别人的名字，是这一动作的机构视角。

branches.en: Military service keeps the same list-making image.
branches.cn: 兵役保留同样的「造册」画面。

branches.en: Joining and being enrolled are two sides of one registration.
branches.cn: 报名与被招收是同一次注册的两面。

branches.en: Courses and armies both work from lists of enrolled names.
branches.cn: 课程与军队都依靠已登记姓名的名单。

intro.en: Enroll is a French-shaped verb built from en- and rolle, a roll or list, with English endings forming its family.
intro.cn: enroll 是法语形态的动词，由 en- 与 rolle（卷册、名册）构成，其词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin rotulus means a little wheel or roll, and Old French rolle turns it into a list of names.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rotulus 意为小轮或卷轴，古法语 rolle 把它变成名册。

items.exampleCN: enroller 把这个动词带入英语。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾
表示被动接受动作的人

definition_zh: 同辈；同龄人；贵族；对等节点；凝视
definition_en: a person of the same age, rank or ability as another; a member of the British nobility; a computer linked to others as an equal; also to look closely at something
core_image: 两个人并肩站在同一级台阶上，谁也不必抬头看谁
scene: 雾很重，站牌上的字迹被水汽糊住，等车的人凑近去看。 Through the fog, he peered at the sign but could not read a word.
sceneCN: 这里是「凝视、仔细看」（第 4 个义项：因看不清而凑近端详）；句意是他在雾里眯眼去看站牌，却一个字也认不出。画面里有浓雾、湿漉漉的站牌与一个前倾的身影。

pos.zh: 同辈；同龄人；贵族；对等节点

derivatives.zh: 由 peer 加表示集体或身份的 -age 构成，义为「贵族阶层；爵位」
由 peer 加表示「没有」的 -less 构成，义为「无与伦比的」
由 peer 与 pressure 复合而成，指同龄群体带来的压力

senses.title: A person of the same age or standing
senses.definition: a person who is the same age as you, or who has the same rank, ability or background
senses.definitionCN: 与你年龄相同，或地位、能力、背景相当的人
senses.example: Teenagers care a lot about the opinion of their peers.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年很在意同龄人的看法。
senses.why: Latin par meant equal, so a peer is first of all someone whose eyes are level with yours, neither above nor below.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 par 意为相等，所以 peer 首先是眼睛与你齐平的人，既不在你之上，也不在你之下。

senses.title: A member of the nobility
senses.definition: a lord who holds a title and, historically, a seat in the upper house of the British parliament
senses.definitionCN: 拥有爵位、历史上在英国上议院拥有席位的贵族
senses.example: The duke took his seat among the peers.
senses.exampleCN: 公爵在众贵族之间就座。
senses.why: Nobles of the same rank called one another equals, and the word for an equal became the name of the rank itself.
senses.whyCN: 同一等级的贵族彼此互称「同等者」，于是表示「同等者」的词就成了这个等级本身的名称。

senses.title: An equal node in a network
senses.definition: a computer or device that exchanges data with others on the same level, without a central server in charge
senses.definitionCN: 在同一层级上与其他设备交换数据、不设中央服务器的计算机或设备
senses.example: Each computer in the network acts as a peer.
senses.exampleCN: 网络中的每台计算机都作为一个对等节点工作。
senses.why: A network without a boss is a network of equals, so the old sense of an equal person was borrowed for machines that talk on equal terms.
senses.whyCN: 没有主控者的网络就是由平等者组成的网络，于是「地位相等的人」这个旧义被借去指平等通信的机器。

senses.title: To look closely at something
senses.definition: to look hard at something, especially when it is difficult to see
senses.definitionCN: 用力地看某物，尤其在不容易看清的时候
senses.example: She peered at the small print without her glasses.
senses.exampleCN: 她没戴眼镜，凑近去看那行小字。
senses.why: This verb is a separate word of uncertain origin; it may be unrelated to the noun, and dictionaries still mark its source as unclear.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是另一个来源不确定的词，可能与名词毫无关系，词典至今仍把它的来源标为不清楚。

intro.en: The noun peer is Latin equality seen through French; the verb peer is a different word whose origin is uncertain, and the two should not be joined.
intro.cn: 名词 peer 是经法语过滤的拉丁语「相等」；动词 peer 则是另一个来源不确定的词，两者不宜混为一谈。

items.en: Par meant equal, and it still survives in English phrases about equality such as on a par with.
items.cn: par 意为相等，至今仍留在 on a par with 这类谈平等的英语说法里。

items.en: Old French per or peer carried the sense of an equal, a person of the same standing.
items.cn: 古法语 per 或 peer 带有「同等者」的意思，指地位相同的人。

items.en: Middle English peer named an equal and, by the late Middle Ages, a noble whose rank set him beside the monarch.
items.cn: 中古英语 peer 指地位相等的人，到中古后期也指其等级可与君主并列的贵族。

items.en: The nobility sense settled in this period, and peerage named the whole body of such nobles.
items.cn: 贵族这一义项在这一时期固定下来，peerage 则指这批贵族的整体。

items.en: Modern English adds the computing sense of an equal machine and keeps the verb peer, whose own source remains uncertain.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「地位对等的机器」这一计算机义，并保留动词 peer；该动词自身的来源仍不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin word for equal; the near-meaning group collects words for an equal person and for steady looking.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「相等」之上的词；近义组收表示地位相同者与稳定注视的词。

entries.definition: The whole body of nobles, or the rank of a peer.
entries.definitionCN: 贵族阶层；或贵族的爵位。

entries.definition: Having no equal; better than all others.
entries.definitionCN: 无与伦比的；无人能及的。

entries.definition: The usual or expected level, from the Latin word for equal.
entries.definitionCN: 通常或预期的水平，来自拉丁语中表示相等的词。

entries.definition: The same in size, value or status.
entries.definitionCN: 在大小、价值或地位上相同的。

entries.definition: A person you work with, often of similar rank.
entries.definitionCN: 与你共事、地位常相近的人。

entries.definition: To look steadily at something for a while.
entries.definitionCN: 稳定地注视某物一段时间。

entries.definition: To look at something for a long time with open eyes.

normalIntro.en: One spelling carries two histories: a noun of equality from Latin, and a verb of looking whose source nobody can name with certainty.
normalIntro.cn: 同一个拼写背着两段历史：来自拉丁语的「平等」名词，以及来源无人能确定的「观看」动词。

normal.en: Peer and par both come from Latin par, so a peer is literally an equal.
normal.cn: peer 与 par 都来自拉丁语 par，所以 peer 字面上就是「相等者」。

normal.en: Peer review works because the judges are equals of the author, not superiors.
normal.cn: 同行评审之所以成立，是因为评审人与作者地位相等，而不是上级。

normal.en: A British peer is noble because such lords once sat as equals beside the monarch.
normal.cn: 英国的 peer 之所以指贵族，是因为这类领主曾以同等者身份与君主同坐。

normal.en: Peer-to-peer networks copy the same idea onto machines that talk without a central server.
normal.cn: 点对点网络把同一想法搬到机器上：无需中央服务器也能彼此通信。

normal.en: The verb peer is a different story: no one knows its origin for certain, so do not link it to the noun.
normal.cn: 动词 peer 是另一回事：没人确知它的来源，所以不要把它和名词挂钩。

abstract.en: A peer is someone whose eyes are level with yours, which is why the word can mean both a companion and a judge.
abstract.cn: peer 是眼睛与你齐平的人，所以这个词既能指同伴，也能指评审者。

abstract.en: Equality is the thread: it holds the schoolmate, the lord and the networked computer together.
abstract.cn: 平等是那条线：它把同学、贵族与联网的计算机串在一起。

abstract.en: The verb peer describes what you do when the world refuses to be clear, and it stands apart from all that equality.
abstract.cn: 动词 peer 描述的是世界不肯清楚时你的动作，它与那一整套平等无关。

examples.en: Children learn a great deal from their peers.
examples.cn: 孩子从同龄人那里学到很多东西。

examples.en: The paper was sent out for peer review before publication.
examples.cn: 这篇论文在发表前被送去同行评审。

examples.en: He peered into the dark room and saw nothing.
examples.cn: 他朝黑屋子里仔细看，什么也没看见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮尔」——同辈人彼此平视，谁也不比谁高；peer 就是同辈。

root: 名词来自拉丁语 par（相等），经古法语 per 或 peer 进入英语，由「同等者」引申出「贵族」与「对等节点」；动词 peer（凝视）来源不确定，一般认为与名词不同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is equality of level; the noun runs from a classmate to a lord to a machine, while the verb takes a separate path and means to look hard.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「高度齐平」；名词从同学走到贵族再走到机器，动词则另走一路，意为用力去看。
